messages:
anya: Heads-up — canary v2 started rolling at 09:05 UTC and we saw error rate tick up on a small subset. Thinking about rollback approach. Prefer fast revert or safe-disable? Also concerned about cached KV / prefix state. 

matt: Can we do a traffic shift back to v1 first? fast and stateless if routing table supports it. :thinking_face: 

anya: Routing supports percent splits and immediate switch. but we have a bunch of per-customer prefixes in the KV cache that v2 primed with new keys (versioned keys). If we flip, some requests will hit stale v1 logic with new cache entries. 

devin: Quick proposal: two-step rollback. 1) block new canary allocation (safe-disable), 2) shift traffic back to baseline 100% (fast revert). The block helps avoid more priming writes while we move traffic. 

rebecca: Agreed. Also recommend running a lightweight invalidation pass for the KV prefixes we control. We have a small script that lists keys with suffix ":v2" and sets a TTL. Prefer TTL approach over mass delete if we suspect cross-version reads. 

matt: Example commands we use for traffic shift (internal API): 

```
POST /internal/rollouts/route
{
  "route": "text.generate",
  "split": {"v1": 100}
}
```

rebecca: For cache: short script: 

```
# mark v2 prefixes to expire in 2m
redis-cli --scan --pattern "cust:*:v2:*" | xargs -L1 redis-cli EXPIRE 120
```

devin: Important guard: first check metric windows for 1-2m after shift, not just deploy success. If we see 5xx spike correlate with shift, revert again and open emergency rollback. 

anya: How do we ensure telemetry doesn't get inflated by the invalidation script? we'd generate a lot of ops. Need to annotate those ops so they don't affect SLO dashboards. 

rebecca: We can emit a special tag header for internal cache ops: X-Internal-Operation: cache-evict and filter it in dashboards. Also add a short-lived metric with name prefix "maintenance." so it doesn't confuse alerting rules. 

deploy-bot: deploy: canary v2 -> 10% on gpu-pool-1 (id: canary-1749864321) 

anya: If we do fast revert, do we also roll back the model artifact in object storage or only routing? My vote: only routing first, avoid touching artifacts unless we confirm corruption. 

matt: +1. Artifacts are read-only; routing flip is atomic and fastest. Artifact rollback should be a separate operation with full audit. 

devin: One edge-case: KV priming that mutated other downstream stores (e.g., user profile enrichment). If v2 wrote new enrichment flags, we might need compensating writes. That is slower and requires a plan per-customer. For now, detect via schema-change-filters in telemetry. 

anya: Ok plan: 
1) safe-disable new canary allocations (prevent further priming). 
2) run targeted TTL-based invalidation for v2 prefixes (emit maintenance tag). 
3) shift 100% traffic back to v1 via internal route API. 
4) monitor error/latency windows for 5 min; if safe, keep disabled and investigate; if not safe, escalate to emergency rollback and run deeper cleanup. 

rebecca: Also add a short-lived console control: "Rollback mode" flag per-route that shows up in the UI so support can see which customers are impacted. That reduces noisy PagerDuty hits. 

matt: Implementation detail: add guard that prevents rolling the canary to 0% if there are in-flight KV mutations older than X seconds. That avoids partial states. We already emit "kv-write-lag" metric per shard. Use that. 

anya: Where do we put the runbook? I'll draft and post to #eng-oncall and link in the console. Quick doc should include commands, who to ping (sre-oncall), and the safe-disable button location. 

devin: SRE note: when you do the redis EXPIRE approach, do it in batches to avoid blocking the server. Use SCAN and sleep 50ms between batches. Also watch RPS. 

sre-oncall: If rollback triggers P0, page me. Also when shifting traffic, make sure we emit a checkpoint event to our tracing system so we can correlate traces before/after. 

anya: thanks all. I'll post the runbook draft in ~20m and kick off the safe-disable now. :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: action: safe-disable applied to canary-1749864321 by anya

rebecca: One more thought — for future rollouts, can we add a cache isolation mode: prefix all writes with rollout id and have read fallback logic that checks rollout-aware key then generic key. That would make revert trivial. But needs client changes. 

matt: That's a good roadmap item. File under "rollouts -> cache isolation" in product tracker. :white_check_mark:

anya: End of thread for now, will update once we finish traffic shift and checks.
